traits.name: Natural Illusionist
traits.effect: You know the Minor Illusion cantrip. Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for it.

traits.name: Speak with Small Beasts
traits.effect: Through sounds and gestures, you can communicate simple ideas with Small or smaller beasts.

traits.name: Gnome Cunning
traits.effect: You have advantage on all Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma saving throws against magic.

traits.name: Nimble Escape
traits.effect: You can take the Disengage or Hide action as a bonus action on each of your turns.

traits.name: Fury of the Small
traits.effect: When you damage a creature larger than you, you can deal extra damage equal to your character level. Once you use this trait, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

traits.name: Stone's Endurance
traits.effect: When you take damage, you can use your reaction to roll 1d12 + your Constitution modifier and reduce the damage by that total (minimum 0). Once you use this trait, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

traits.name: Powerful Build
traits.effect: You count as one size larger when determining your carrying capacity and the weight you can push, drag, or lift.

traits.name: Natural Athlete
traits.effect: Proficiency in the Athletics skill.

traits.name: Mountain Born
traits.effect: You have resistance to cold damage. You’re also acclimated to high altitude, including elevations above 20,000 feet.

traits.name: Skills
traits.effect: You gain proficiency in one skill of your choice.

traits.name: Feat
traits.effect: You gain one feat of your choice.

traits.name: Daunting Roar
traits.effect: As a bonus action, unleash a terrifying roar. Each creature of your choice within 10 feet of you that can hear you must succeed on a Constitution saving throw (DC 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Constitution modifier) or become frightened of you until the end of your next turn. Once used, you can't use this trait again until you finish a short or long rest.

traits.name: Claws
traits.effect: Your claws are natural weapons, which you can use to make unarmed strikes. On a hit, they deal slashing damage equal to 1d4 + your Strength modifier, instead of the bludgeoning damage normal for an unarmed strike.

traits.name: Hunter's Instincts
traits.effect: Proficiency in one skill of your choice: Athletics, Intimidation, Perception, or Survival.

traits.name: Lucky
traits.effect: When you roll a 1 on the d20 for an attack roll, ability check, or saving throw, you can reroll the die and must use the new roll.

traits.name: Brave
traits.effect: Advantage on saving throws against being frightened.

traits.name: Halfling Nimbleness
traits.effect: You can move through the space of any creature that is of a size larger than yours.

traits.name: Stout Resilience
traits.effect: Advantage on saving throws against poison and resistance to poison damage.

traits.name: Lucky
traits.effect: When you roll a 1 on the d20 for an attack roll, ability check, or saving throw, you can reroll the die and must use the new roll.

traits.name: Brave
traits.effect: Advantage on saving throws against being frightened.

traits.name: Halfling Nimbleness
traits.effect: You can move through the space of any creature that is of a size larger than yours.

traits.name: Naturally Stealthy
traits.effect: You can attempt to hide even when you are obscured only by a creature that is at least one size larger than you.

traits.name: Fey Ancestry
traits.effect: You have advantage on saving throws against being charmed, and magic can't put you to sleep.

traits.name: Skill Versatility
traits.effect: Proficiency in 2 skills of choice

traits.name: Relentless Endurance
traits.effect: When you are reduced to 0 hit points but not killed outright, you can drop to 1 hit point instead. Once you use this trait, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.

traits.name: Savage Attacks
traits.effect: When you score a critical hit with a melee weapon attack, you can roll one of the weapon's damage dice one additional time and add it to the extra damage of the critical hit.

traits.name: Menacing
traits.effect: Proficiency in the Intimidation skill.

traits.name: Feline Agility
traits.effect: When you move on your turn in combat, you can double your speed until the end of the turn. Once you use this trait, you can't use it again until you move 0 feet on one of your turns.

traits.name: Cat's Claws
traits.effect: You have a climbing speed of 20 feet. Your claws are natural weapons that you can use to make unarmed strikes; on a hit, they deal slashing damage equal to 1d4 + your Strength modifier instead of the bludgeoning damage normal for an unarmed strike.

traits.name: Cat's Talent
traits.effect: Proficiency in the Perception and Stealth skills.

traits.name: Hellish Resistance
traits.effect: Resistance to fire damage

traits.name: Infernal Legacy
traits.effect: You know the Thaumaturgy cantrip. At 3rd level, you can cast Hellish Rebuke as a 2nd-level spell once with this trait; at 5th level, you can cast Darkness once with this trait. You regain each spell use when you finish a long rest. Charisma is your spellcasting ability for these spells.

features.description: Gain proficiency with the disguise kit and poisoner's kit.
You have advantage on attack rolls against creatures that have not yet taken a turn in combat; hits against a surprised creature are critical hits.

You can create a false identity for yourself. You must spend seven days and 25 gp to establish the history, profession, and affiliations for the identity. You cannot establish an identity that belongs to someone else. For example, you might acquire appropriate clothing, letters of introduction, and official-looking certification to establish yourself as a member of a trading house from a remote city. Thereafter, if you adopt the new identity as a disguise, other creatures believe you to be that person until given an obvious reason not to.

You can unfailingly imitate another person's speech, writing, and behavior. You must spend at least three hours studying these three elements of the person's behavior: listening to the person speak, examining the person's handwriting, and observing the person's mannerisms. Your ruse is indiscernible to the casual observer. If a wary creature suspects something is amiss, you have advantage on any Charisma (Deception) check you make to avoid detection.

When you hit a surprised creature with an attack, it must make a Constitution saving throw (DC 8 + your Dexterity modifier + your proficiency bonus). On a failed save, double the damage of your attack against it.

At fighter level 3, learn two wizard cantrips and three 1st-level wizard spells; two spells must be from abjuration or evocation, while the third can be from any school. Learn one additional wizard cantrip of your choice at fighter level 10. Later wizard spells you learn must be from abjuration or evocation, except spells learned at fighter levels 8, 14, and 20, which can come from any school. When replacing a known spell as you gain a fighter level, the replacement must be abjuration or evocation unless you are replacing the any-school spell gained at fighter level 3, 8, 14, or 20. Intelligence is your spellcasting ability. Spell slots and known-spell progression follow the 2014 Eldritch Knight table; regain expended slots after a long rest.

At 3rd level, learn a ritual that creates a magical bond between yourself and one weapon. Perform the ritual over 1 hour; it can take place during a short rest, and the weapon must remain within your reach throughout. At the end of the ritual, touch the weapon to forge the bond. You cannot be disarmed of a bonded weapon unless incapacitated. If it is on the same plane of existence, you can summon it to your hand as a bonus action, causing it to teleport instantly. You can bond with up to two weapons, but can summon only one of them at a time with that bonus action. If you bond with a third weapon, you must break the bond with one of the other two.
When you use your action to cast a cantrip, you can make one weapon attack as a bonus action.
When you hit a creature with a weapon attack, it has disadvantage on the next saving throw it makes against a spell you cast before the end of your next turn.
When you use Action Surge, you can teleport up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space you can see. You can teleport before or after the additional action.
When you use your action to cast a spell, you can make one weapon attack as a bonus action.

When you hit a creature with one of the attacks granted by Flurry of Blows, you can impose one of three effects: it must make a Dexterity save or be knocked prone, make a Strength save or be pushed up to 15 feet, or it cannot take reactions until the end of your next turn.
As an action, regain hit points equal to three times your monk level. Once used, this feature recharges after a long rest.
At the end of a long rest, gain the effect of the sanctuary spell until the start of your next long rest; it can end early as normal. The save DC is 8 + your Wisdom modifier + proficiency bonus.

When you hit a creature with an unarmed strike, you can spend 3 ki points to start imperceptible vibrations lasting for a number of days equal to your monk level. The vibrations are harmless until you use your action to end them; you and the target must be on the same plane of existence. The target makes a Constitution saving throw. On a failure, it is reduced to 0 hit points; on a success, it takes 10d10 necrotic damage. Only one creature can be affected at a time. You can end the vibrations harmlessly without an action.

As an action, you can spend 2 ki points to cast darkness, darkvision, pass without trace, or silence without providing material components. You also learn the minor illusion cantrip if you do not already know it.

While you are in dim light or darkness, you can use a bonus action to teleport up to 60 feet to an unoccupied space you can see that is also in dim light or darkness. You then have advantage on the first melee attack you make before the end of the current turn.
When you are in an area of dim light or darkness, you can use your action to become invisible. You remain invisible until you make an attack, cast a spell, or enter an area of bright light.
Whenever a creature within 5 feet of you is hit by an attack made by a creature other than you, you can use your reaction to make a melee attack against that creature.

At 3rd level, you learn Elemental Attunement and one other elemental discipline of your choice. You learn one additional discipline of your choice at monk levels 6, 11, and 17; whenever you learn a discipline, you can replace one discipline you already know with a different one. Elemental Attunement costs no ki; each other discipline lists its ki cost and any level prerequisite. For discipline spells, use the spell's casting time and rules, but you do not need to provide material components. Starting at monk level 5, when a discipline lets you cast a spell that has an enhanced effect at a higher level, you can spend additional ki to increase its spell level by 1 for each additional ki point. The total ki spent on such a spell, including its base cost, is capped at 3 for monk levels 5–8, 4 for levels 9–12, 5 for levels 13–16, and 6 for levels 17–20.

As an action, control elemental forces within 30 feet to create one effect: a harmless instantaneous sensory effect related to air, earth, fire, or water; instantly light or snuff out a candle, torch, or small campfire; chill or warm up to 1 pound of nonliving material for up to 1 hour; or shape earth, fire, water, or mist that fits within a 1-foot cube into a crude form for 1 minute. This discipline costs no ki.

name.es: Colmillos de la Serpiente de Fuego

features.description: When you take the Attack action on your turn, you can spend 1 ki point to extend your unarmed-strike reach by 10 feet for that action and the rest of the turn, as tendrils of flame stretch from your fists and feet. Hits with those unarmed strikes deal fire damage instead of bludgeoning damage. When one of those attacks hits, you can spend 1 additional ki point to deal an extra 1d10 fire damage.
Spend 2 ki points to cast thunderwave.

As an action, spend 2 ki points and choose a creature within 30 feet. It must make a Strength saving throw. On a failure, it takes 3d10 bludgeoning damage plus 1d10 for each additional ki point you spend, and you can push it up to 20 feet away and knock it prone. On a success, it takes half as much damage and is neither pushed nor knocked prone.

As an action, spend 1 ki point and choose an area of ice or water no larger than 30 feet on a side within 120 feet. You can change water to ice within the area and vice versa, and reshape ice as you choose, including raising or lowering it, creating or filling a trench, making a wall, or forming a pillar. The extent of a change cannot exceed half the area's largest dimension. You cannot shape the ice to trap or injure a creature in the area.
Spend 2 ki points to cast burning hands.

As an action, spend 2 ki points to create a whip of water and choose a creature you can see within 30 feet. It makes a Dexterity saving throw. On a failure, it takes 3d10 bludgeoning damage plus 1d10 for each additional ki point you spend, and you either knock it prone or pull it up to 25 feet closer to you. On a success, it takes half as much damage and is neither pulled nor knocked prone.

name.es: Arremetida de los Espíritus del Vendaval

features.description: Spend 2 ki points to cast gust of wind.

Learn one additional elemental discipline of your choice; you may replace one discipline you already know with another when learning it. The ki-cost ceiling for scaling elemental spells is based on monk level, not on the number of disciplines known.
Prerequisite: 6th level in this class. Spend 3 ki points to cast hold person.
Prerequisite: 6th level in this class. Spend 3 ki points to cast shatter.
Learn one additional elemental discipline of your choice; you may replace one discipline you already know with another when learning it.
Prerequisite: 11th level in this class. Spend 4 ki points to cast fireball.
Prerequisite: 11th level in this class. Spend 4 ki points to cast gaseous form, targeting yourself.
Prerequisite: 11th level in this class. Spend 4 ki points to cast fly, targeting yourself.
Learn one additional elemental discipline of your choice; you may replace one discipline you already know with another when learning it.
Prerequisite: 17th level in this class. Spend 6 ki points to cast cone of cold.
Prerequisite: 17th level in this class. Spend 5 ki points to cast stoneskin, targeting yourself.
Prerequisite: 17th level in this class. Spend 5 ki points to cast wall of fire.
Prerequisite: 17th level in this class. Spend 6 ki points to cast wall of stone.
Weapon attacks score a critical hit on a roll of 19 or 20.

Add half your proficiency bonus (rounded up) to Strength, Dexterity, or Constitution checks that do not already include your proficiency bonus. Your running long-jump distance also increases by your Strength modifier in feet.
Choose a second option from the fighter's Fighting Style feature.
Your weapon attacks score a critical hit on a roll of 18–20.
At the start of each of your turns, regain 5 + your Constitution modifier hit points if you have no more than half your hit points remaining and at least 1 hit point.

At 3rd level, choose one option. Colossus Slayer: when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, it takes an extra 1d8 damage if it is below its hit point maximum; this extra damage applies only once per turn. Giant Killer: when a Large or larger creature within 5 feet hits or misses you with an attack, you can use your reaction to attack it immediately after its attack, provided you can see it. Horde Breaker: once on each of your turns when you make a weapon attack, you can make one additional attack with the same weapon against a different creature within 5 feet of the original target and within your weapon's range.

Choose one option: Escape the Horde gives opportunity attacks against you disadvantage; Multiattack Defense grants +4 AC against subsequent attacks from a creature that hit you for the rest of that turn; Steel Will grants advantage on saves against being frightened.

At 11th level, choose one option. Volley: use your action to make a ranged attack against any number of creatures within 10 feet of a point you can see within your weapon's range. Make a separate attack roll for each target and have ammunition for each, as normal. Whirlwind Attack: use your action to make melee attacks against any number of creatures within 5 feet of you, with a separate attack roll for each target.

At 15th level, choose one option. Evasion: when an effect lets you make a Dexterity saving throw to take half damage, you take no damage on a success and half damage on a failure. Stand Against the Tide: when a hostile creature misses you with a melee attack, you can use your reaction to force it to repeat the same attack against another creature of your choice other than itself. Uncanny Dodge: when an attacker you can see hits you with an attack, you can use your reaction to halve the attack's damage against you.

You can use Wild Shape as a bonus action instead of an action. While transformed by Wild Shape, you can use a bonus action and expend one spell slot to regain 1d8 hit points per level of the slot expended.

At 2nd level, you can Wild Shape into a beast with challenge rating up to 1, ignoring the Beast Shapes table's maximum-CR column but obeying its other limitations: you cannot choose a form with a swimming speed before druid level 4 or a flying speed before druid level 8. Starting at druid level 6, the maximum challenge rating becomes one-third your druid level, rounded down.
Your attacks in beast form count as magical for overcoming resistance and immunity to nonmagical attacks and damage.

At druid level 10, you can expend two uses of Wild Shape at the same time to transform into an air, earth, fire, or water elemental. This elemental transformation uses the elemental form options granted by this feature rather than the beast challenge-rating limit of Circle Forms.
Cast alter self at will.
Learn one additional druid cantrip of your choice; it does not count against the number of druid cantrips you know.

Once per long rest, when you finish a short rest, choose expended spell slots to recover. The slots can have a combined level no greater than half your druid level (rounded up), and none can be 6th level or higher.

Choose the land where you became a druid: arctic, coast, desert, forest, grassland, mountain, swamp, or Underdark. The listed circle spells become always prepared at the listed druid levels and do not count against the number of spells you can prepare; if a spell is not normally on the druid spell list, it is still a druid spell for you. Arctic: level 3 hold person, spike growth; level 5 sleet storm, slow; level 7 freedom of movement, ice storm; level 9 commune with nature, cone of cold. Coast: level 3 mirror image, misty step; level 5 water breathing, water walk; level 7 control water, freedom of movement; level 9 conjure elemental, scrying. Desert: level 3 blur, silence; level 5 create food and water, protection from energy; level 7 blight, hallucinatory terrain; level 9 insect plague, wall of stone. Forest: level 3 barkskin, spider climb; level 5 call lightning, plant growth; level 7 divination, freedom of movement; level 9 commune with nature, tree stride. Grassland: level 3 invisibility, pass without trace; level 5 daylight, haste; level 7 divination, freedom of movement; level 9 dream, insect plague. Mountain: level 3 spider climb, spike growth; level 5 lightning bolt, meld into stone; level 7 stone shape, stoneskin; level 9 passwall, wall of stone. Swamp: level 3 darkness, Melf's acid arrow; level 5 water walk, stinking cloud; level 7 freedom of movement, locate creature; level 9 insect plague, scrying. Underdark: level 3 spider climb, web; level 5 gaseous form, stinking cloud; level 7 greater invisibility, stone shape; level 9 cloudkill, insect plague.

Moving through nonmagical difficult terrain costs you no extra movement. You can also pass through nonmagical plants without being slowed or taking damage from their thorns, spines, or similar hazards. You have advantage on saves against plants that are magically created or manipulated to impede movement.
You cannot be charmed or frightened by elementals or fey, and you are immune to poison and disease.

When a beast or plant creature attacks you, it must make a Wisdom saving throw against your druid spell save DC. On a failure, it must choose another target or the attack misses; on a success, it is immune to this feature for 24 hours. The creature is aware of this effect before it attacks.
Gain proficiency in three skills of your choice.

As a reaction, when a creature you can see within 60 feet makes an attack roll, ability check, or damage roll, you can expend one use of Bardic Inspiration, roll the Bardic Inspiration die, and subtract the result from the creature's roll. You can decide after the creature rolls but before the DM determines whether an attack roll or ability check succeeds or fails, or before the creature deals its damage. The creature must be able to hear you and cannot be immune to being charmed.

At bard level 6, learn two spells of your choice from any class. Each spell must be a cantrip or of a level you can cast, as shown on the bard table. The chosen spells count as bard spells for you, but they do not count against the number of bard spells you know.

When you make an ability check, you can expend one use of Bardic Inspiration and add the Bardic Inspiration die to the check. You can decide after rolling the ability check, but before the DM says whether it succeeds or fails.
Gain proficiency with medium armor, shields, and martial weapons.

A creature that has one of your Bardic Inspiration dice can roll it and add the result to a weapon damage roll it has just made. Alternatively, when an attack roll is made against it, the creature can use its reaction to roll the die and add the result to its AC against that attack, after seeing the attack roll but before knowing whether it hits or misses.
You can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.
When you use your action to cast a bard spell, you can make one weapon attack as a bonus action on the same turn.
Gain proficiency with martial weapons and heavy armor.

When you use the Attack action on your turn, you can make one weapon attack as a bonus action. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (a minimum of once). You regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

name.es: Conjuros del Dominio de la Guerra

features.description: You always have the domain spells prepared, and they do not count against the number of cleric spells you can prepare: cleric level 1: divine favor, shield of faith; level 3: magic weapon, spiritual weapon; level 5: crusader's mantle, spirit guardians; level 7: freedom of movement, stoneskin; level 9: flame strike, hold monster. If a spell does not normally appear on the cleric spell list, it is a cleric spell for you.
When you make an attack roll, you can use Channel Divinity after seeing the roll but before the DM says whether it hits to gain a +10 bonus to that roll.

name.es: Canalizar Divinidad: Bendición del Dios de la Guerra

features.description: When a creature within 30 feet of you makes an attack roll, you can use your reaction to expend Channel Divinity and grant it a +10 bonus to the roll. You can choose to use this after seeing the roll but before the DM says whether it hits.

Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can cause the attack to deal an extra 1d8 damage of the same type dealt by the weapon to the target. When you reach cleric level 14, the extra damage increases to 2d8.
Gain resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks.
Learn the light cantrip if you do not already know it. This cantrip does not count against the number of cleric cantrips you know.

When a creature you can see within 30 feet attacks you, use your reaction to impose disadvantage on that attack roll. An attacker that cannot be blinded is immune to this feature. You can use it a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum once), and regain all uses after a long rest.

name.es: Conjuros del Dominio de la Luz

features.description: You always have the domain spells prepared, and they do not count against the number of cleric spells you can prepare: cleric level 1: burning hands, faerie fire; level 3: flaming sphere, scorching ray; level 5: daylight, fireball; level 7: guardian of faith, wall of fire; level 9: flame strike, scrying. If a spell does not normally appear on the cleric spell list, it is a cleric spell for you.

name.en: Channel Divinity: Radiance of the Dawn

features.description: As an action, use your Channel Divinity and present your holy symbol to dispel any magical darkness within 30 feet and deal radiant damage to each hostile creature within 30 feet that is not behind total cover. Each affected creature makes a Constitution saving throw, taking 2d10 + your cleric level radiant damage on a failure, or half as much on a success. The feature dispels magical darkness without a spell-level threshold.
You can use Warding Flare when a creature you can see within 30 feet attacks another creature.
Add your Wisdom modifier to the damage you deal with cleric cantrips.

As an action, activate an aura of sunlight that lasts 1 minute or until you dismiss it using another action. You emit bright light in a 60-foot radius and dim light for an additional 30 feet. Your enemies in the bright light have disadvantage on saving throws against any spell that deals fire or radiant damage.

Learn one druid cantrip of your choice. This cantrip counts as a cleric cantrip for you, but it does not count against the number of cleric cantrips you know. You also gain proficiency in one of the following skills of your choice: Animal Handling, Nature, or Survival.
Gain proficiency with heavy armor.

name.es: Conjuros del Dominio de la Naturaleza

features.description: You always have the domain spells prepared, and they do not count against the number of cleric spells you can prepare: cleric level 1: animal friendship, speak with animals; level 3: barkskin, spike growth; level 5: plant growth, wind wall; level 7: dominate beast, grasping vine; level 9: insect plague, tree stride. If a spell does not normally appear on the cleric spell list, it is a cleric spell for you.

name.en: Channel Divinity: Charm Animals and Plants
name.es: Canalizar Divinidad: Encantar Animales y Plantas

features.description: As an action, use Channel Divinity to present your holy symbol and invoke the name of your deity. Each beast or plant creature within 30 feet that can see you must make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, it is charmed by you for 1 minute or until it takes damage. While charmed this way, it is friendly to you and to creatures you designate.
When you or a creature within 30 feet takes acid, cold, fire, lightning, or thunder damage, use your reaction to grant that creature resistance to that instance of damage.

Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can cause the attack to deal an extra 1d8 cold, fire, or lightning damage (your choice) to the target. When you reach cleric level 14, the extra damage increases to 2d8.
While creatures are charmed by your Channel Divinity: Charm Animals and Plants, you can take a bonus action on your turn to verbally command what each of those creatures will do on its next turn.
Gain proficiency with martial weapons and heavy armor.

When a creature you can see within 5 feet hits you with an attack, use your reaction to make it attempt a Dexterity saving throw. It takes 2d8 lightning or thunder damage (your choice) on a failed save, or half as much on a success. Uses equal your Wisdom modifier (minimum one); regain all uses after a long rest.

name.es: Conjuros del Dominio de la Tempestad

features.description: You always have the domain spells prepared, and they do not count against the number of cleric spells you can prepare: cleric level 1: fog cloud, thunderwave; level 3: gust of wind, shatter; level 5: call lightning, sleet storm; level 7: control water, ice storm; level 9: destructive wave, insect plague. If a spell does not normally appear on the cleric spell list, it is a cleric spell for you.
When you roll lightning or thunder damage, you can use Channel Divinity to deal maximum damage instead of rolling. Apply this to the damage roll's dice; it does not require an action.
When you deal lightning damage to a Large or smaller creature, you can also push it up to 10 feet away from you.

Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can cause the attack to deal an extra 1d8 thunder damage to the target. When you reach cleric level 14, the extra damage increases to 2d8.
At cleric level 17, you gain a flying speed equal to your current walking speed whenever you are neither underground nor indoors.
Gain proficiency with heavy armor.
When you use a spell of 1st level or higher to restore hit points to a creature, it regains additional hit points equal to 2 + the spell's level.

name.es: Conjuros del Dominio de la Vida

features.description: You always have the domain spells prepared at the cleric levels shown by the 2014 Life Domain table: 1st bless and cure wounds; 3rd lesser restoration and spiritual weapon; 5th beacon of hope and revivify; 7th death ward and guardian of faith; 9th mass cure wounds and raise dead. These spells do not count against your prepared cleric spells. If a spell does not normally appear on the cleric spell list, it is a cleric spell for you.

As an action, use your Channel Divinity to evoke healing energy and distribute hit points equal to five times your cleric level among creatures you choose within 30 feet. No creature can be healed above half its hit point maximum; this feature cannot affect undead or constructs.
When you cast a spell of 1st level or higher that restores hit points to a creature other than you, you regain hit points equal to 2 + the spell's level.
Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, deal an extra 1d8 radiant damage. At cleric level 14, the extra damage becomes 2d8.
When you would normally roll one or more dice to restore hit points with a spell, use the maximum possible result for each die.

At cleric level 1, learn two languages of your choice. You also become proficient in two of the following skills of your choice: Arcana, History, Nature, or Religion. Your proficiency bonus is doubled for any ability check you make that uses either of those skill proficiencies.

You always have the domain spells prepared, and they do not count against the number of cleric spells you can prepare: cleric level 1: command, identify; level 3: augury, suggestion; level 5: nondetection, speak with dead; level 7: arcane eye, confusion; level 9: legend lore, scrying. If a spell does not normally appear on the cleric spell list, it is a cleric spell for you.
As an action, use Channel Divinity to gain proficiency in one skill or tool for 10 minutes.

As an action, use Channel Divinity to choose one creature you can see within 60 feet; it makes a Wisdom saving throw. On a success, you cannot use this feature on it again until you finish a long rest. On a failure, the effect lasts for 1 minute, during which you can read the creature's surface thoughts whenever it is within 60 feet of you. During that time, you can use your action to end the effect and cast suggestion on it without a spell slot; the target automatically fails that spell's saving throw.
Add your Wisdom modifier to the damage you deal with cleric cantrips.

Meditate and pray for at least 1 minute, maintaining concentration as if concentrating on a spell. You can meditate for a number of minutes equal to your Wisdom score. After using this feature, you cannot use it again until a short or long rest. Object Reading: while holding an object, after 1 minute you learn how its previous owner acquired and lost it and the most recent significant event involving the object and that owner. If the object was owned by another creature within a number of days equal to your Wisdom score, you can spend 1 additional minute per previous owner to learn the same information about that creature. Area Reading: perceive significant events in an area up to a 50-foot cube, going back a number of days equal to your Wisdom score; each minute reveals one significant event, starting with the most recent.
As an action, touch a willing creature other than yourself to grant advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks for 1 hour or until you use this feature again.

You always have the domain spells prepared, and they do not count against the number of cleric spells you can prepare: cleric level 1: charm person, disguise self; level 3: mirror image, pass without trace; level 5: blink, dispel magic; level 7: dimension door, polymorph; level 9: dominate person, modify memory. If a spell does not normally appear on the cleric spell list, it is a cleric spell for you.

As an action, use your Channel Divinity to create a perfect illusory duplicate of yourself in an unoccupied space you can see within 30 feet. The illusion lasts up to 1 minute while you maintain concentration as if concentrating on a spell. As a bonus action on your turn, you can move it up to 30 feet to a space you can see, but it must remain within 120 feet of you. For the duration, you can cast spells as though you were in the illusion's space, using your own senses. In addition, when both you and the illusion are within 5 feet of a creature that can see the illusion, you have advantage on attack rolls against that creature.
As an action, use Channel Divinity to become invisible until the end of your next turn. You become visible if you attack or cast a spell.

Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can cause the attack to deal an extra 1d8 poison damage to the target. When you reach cleric level 14, the extra damage increases to 2d8.
When you use Invoke Duplicity, you can create up to four duplicates instead of one. As a bonus action, move any number of them up to 30 feet each, keeping them within 120 feet of you.

The Archfey adds these spells as options when learning warlock spells: 1st faerie fire, sleep; 2nd calm emotions, phantasmal force; 3rd blink, plant growth; 4th dominate beast, greater invisibility; 5th dominate person, seeming. These spells are added to the warlock spell list for you but are not automatically known; you can choose them when you learn warlock spells.

As an action, each creature in a 10-foot cube originating from you makes a Wisdom saving throw against your warlock spell save DC. Choose whether creatures that fail are charmed or frightened by you until the end of your next turn; the same condition applies to all creatures that fail this use. Once used, recharge after a short or long rest.

When you take damage, you can use your reaction to turn invisible and teleport up to 60 feet to an unoccupied space you can see. You remain invisible until the start of your next turn or until you attack or cast a spell. Recharge after a short or long rest.

You are immune to being charmed. When another creature attempts to charm you, you can use your reaction to make it attempt a Wisdom saving throw against your warlock spell save DC; on a failure, it is charmed by you for 1 minute or until it takes any damage.

As an action, choose a creature you can see within 60 feet. It makes a Wisdom saving throw against your warlock spell save DC; on a failure, it is charmed or frightened by you (your choice) for up to 1 minute or until your concentration is broken, as if concentrating on a spell. This effect ends early if the target takes any damage. Until this illusion ends, the target thinks it is lost in a misty realm of your choice and can see and hear only itself, you, and the illusion. Recharge after a short or long rest.
When you reduce a hostile creature to 0 hit points, gain temporary hit points equal to your Charisma modifier + your warlock level (minimum 1 temporary hit point).

The Fiend adds these spells as options when you learn warlock spells: 1st burning hands, command; 2nd blindness/deafness, scorching ray; 3rd fireball, stinking cloud; 4th fire shield, wall of fire; 5th flame strike, hallow. These spells are added to the warlock spell list for you but are not automatically known; you can choose them when you learn warlock spells.
When you make an ability check or saving throw, add 1d10 to the roll after seeing the initial roll but before its effects occur. Once used, recharge after a short or long rest.

When you finish a short or long rest, choose one damage type. You gain resistance to that damage type until you choose a different one with this feature. Damage from magical weapons or silver weapons ignores this resistance.

When you hit a creature with an attack, you can send it momentarily through the lower planes. The target disappears and returns to the space it left, or the nearest unoccupied space, at the end of your next turn. If the target is not a fiend, it takes 10d10 psychic damage when it returns. Once used, recharge after a long rest.

At rogue level 3, learn mage hand and two other wizard cantrips, plus three 1st-level wizard spells; two spells must be enchantment or illusion, while the third can be from any school. Learn one additional wizard cantrip at rogue level 10. Later wizard spells you learn must be enchantment or illusion, except spells learned at rogue levels 8, 14, and 20, which can come from any school. When replacing a known spell as you gain a rogue level, the replacement must be enchantment or illusion unless you are replacing the any-school spell gained at rogue level 3, 8, 14, or 20. Intelligence is your spellcasting ability; spell slots and spells known follow the 2014 Arcane Trickster table, and expended slots return after a long rest.

name.es: Juego de Manos con Mano de Mago

features.description: When you cast mage hand, you can make the spectral hand invisible, and you can perform these additional tasks with it: stow one object the hand is holding in a container worn or carried by another creature; retrieve an object from a container worn or carried by another creature; or use thieves' tools to pick locks and disarm traps at range. You can perform one of these tasks without being noticed if you succeed on a Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) check contested by the observer's Wisdom (Perception) check. In addition, you can use the bonus action granted by Cunning Action to control the hand.
If you are hidden from a creature when you cast a spell on it, it has disadvantage on saving throws against that spell this turn.
As a bonus action, direct your mage hand to distract a creature within 5 feet of it, granting you advantage on attack rolls against that creature until the end of the turn.

Immediately after a creature casts a spell that targets you or includes you in its area of effect, you can use your reaction to force the caster to make a saving throw using its own spellcasting ability modifier against your spell save DC. On a failure, you negate the spell's effect against you. If the spell is at least 1st level and of a level you can cast, you learn it for 8 hours and can cast it using your spell slots; the caster cannot cast that spell during those 8 hours. Once you use this feature, you cannot use it again until you finish a long rest.
The gold and time you must spend to copy an abjuration spell into your spellbook are halved.

When you cast an abjuration spell of 1st level or higher, you can simultaneously use a strand of the spell's magic to create a magical ward on yourself that lasts until you finish a long rest. The ward has hit points equal to twice your wizard level + your Intelligence modifier. Whenever you take damage, the ward takes the damage instead; if this damage reduces the ward to 0 hit points, you take any remaining damage. While the ward has 0 hit points, it cannot absorb damage, but its magic remains. Whenever you cast an abjuration spell of 1st level or higher, the ward regains hit points equal to twice the level of the spell. Once you create the ward, you cannot create it again until you finish a long rest.

When a creature you can see within 30 feet takes damage, you can use your reaction to have your Arcane Ward absorb that damage instead. If the ward is reduced to 0 hit points, the creature takes any remaining damage.
When you cast an abjuration spell that requires you to make an ability check as part of casting it, add your proficiency bonus to that check.
You have advantage on saving throws against spells and resistance to damage from spells.
The gold and time you must spend to copy a divination spell into your spellbook are halved.

When you finish a long rest, roll two d20s and record the results. Before a roll is made, you can replace an attack roll, saving throw, or ability check made by you or a creature you can see with one recorded result. Each result can be used once, and you can replace a roll only once per turn. Unused results are lost when you finish your next long rest.

When you cast a divination spell of 2nd level or higher using a spell slot, regain one expended spell slot. The recovered slot must be lower level than the spell cast and cannot be higher than 5th level.

As an action, choose one benefit: darkvision 60 feet, sight into the Ethereal Plane within 60 feet, ability to read any language, or sight of invisible creatures and objects within 10 feet that are in your line of sight. The benefit lasts until you are incapacitated or take a short or long rest. After using this feature, you cannot use it again until you finish a short or long rest.
Roll three d20s for Portent after finishing a long rest instead of two.
The gold and time you must spend to copy a conjuration spell into your spellbook are halved.

As an action, conjure in your hand or in an unoccupied space you can see within 10 feet one inanimate, nonmagical object you have seen before. It must fit entirely within a 3-foot cube and weigh no more than 10 pounds. The object is visibly magical and sheds dim light out to 5 feet. It disappears after 1 hour, when you use this feature again, or if it takes or deals any damage.

As an action, teleport up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space you can see. Alternatively, choose a space within 30 feet occupied by a Small or Medium creature. If that creature is willing, you and the creature teleport, swapping positions. Once you use this feature, you cannot use it again until you finish a long rest or cast a conjuration spell of 1st level or higher.
While you are concentrating on a conjuration spell, taking damage cannot break your concentration.
Any creature you summon or create with a conjuration spell has 30 temporary hit points.
The gold and time you must spend to copy an enchantment spell into your spellbook are halved.

As an action, choose a creature you can see within 5 feet. If it can see or hear you, it must succeed on a Wisdom save against your wizard spell save DC or be charmed until the end of your next turn; its speed becomes 0 and it is incapacitated and visibly dazed. On later turns, you can use your action to extend the effect until the end of your next turn. The effect ends if you move more than 5 feet away, the creature can neither see nor hear you, or it takes damage. If it ends or the target succeeds on its initial save, you cannot use this feature on that creature again until you finish a long rest.

When a creature you can see within 30 feet makes an attack roll against you, use your reaction before knowing whether it hits or misses, provided another creature is within the attack's range. The attacker makes a Wisdom save against your wizard spell save DC; on a failure, it must target the creature closest to it other than you or itself, choosing among ties. Creatures that cannot be charmed are immune. If the attacker succeeds, you cannot use this feature on it again until you finish a long rest.
When you cast an enchantment spell of 1st level or higher that targets only one creature, you can have it target a second creature within range.

At 14th level, when you cast an enchantment spell that charms one or more creatures, you can alter one creature's understanding so that it remains unaware of having been charmed. Once before the spell expires, you can use your action to try to make the chosen creature forget some of the time it spent charmed. The creature must make an Intelligence saving throw against your wizard spell save DC; on a failure, it loses a number of hours of memories equal to 1 + your Charisma modifier (minimum 1). You can choose a shorter period, but it cannot exceed the duration of your enchantment spell.
The gold and time you must spend to copy an evocation spell into your spellbook are halved.

When you cast an evocation spell that affects other creatures you can see, you can choose a number of them equal to 1 + the spell's level. The chosen creatures automatically succeed on their saving throws against the spell, and they take no damage if they would normally take half damage on a successful save.
When a creature succeeds on a saving throw against one of your damaging cantrips, it takes half the cantrip's damage (if any) but suffers no additional effect from the cantrip.
Add your Intelligence modifier (minimum +1) to one damage roll of any wizard evocation spell you cast.

When you cast a wizard spell of 1st through 5th level that deals damage, you can deal maximum damage with that spell. The first use before finishing a long rest causes no self-damage. Starting with the second use, immediately after casting the spell you take 2d12 necrotic damage per spell level; this damage ignores resistance and immunity. Each further use before finishing a long rest increases the necrotic damage by 1d12 per spell level.
The gold and time you must spend to copy an illusion spell into your spellbook are halved.

Learn the minor illusion cantrip. If you already know it, learn a different wizard cantrip of your choice instead. Minor illusion does not count against the number of wizard cantrips you know. When you cast it, you can create both a sound and an image with a single casting.

Starting at 6th level, when you cast an illusion spell with a duration of 1 minute or longer, you can use your action to change the nature of that illusion, provided you can see it and the spell's normal parameters allow the change.

When a creature makes an attack roll against you, use your reaction to interpose an illusory duplicate between you and the attacker. The attack automatically misses you, then the duplicate dissipates. Once used, recharge after a short or long rest.

When you cast an illusion spell of 1st level or higher, you can choose one inanimate, nonmagical object that is part of the illusion and make it real as a bonus action on your turn while the spell is ongoing. The object remains real for 1 minute and cannot deal damage or otherwise directly harm anyone.
The gold and time you must spend to copy a necromancy spell into your spellbook are halved.

Once per turn, when you kill one or more creatures with a spell of 1st level or higher, regain hit points equal to twice the spell's level, or three times its level if the spell is a necromancy spell. You do not gain this healing from killing constructs or undead.

Add animate dead to your spellbook if it is not already there. When you cast animate dead, you can target one additional corpse or pile of bones, creating one additional zombie or skeleton, as appropriate. Undead you create with a necromancy spell have their hit point maximum increased by an amount equal to your wizard level and add your proficiency bonus to their weapon damage rolls.
Gain resistance to necrotic damage and your hit point maximum cannot be reduced.

As an action, choose one undead you can see within 60 feet; it makes a Charisma saving throw against your wizard spell save DC. If it succeeds, you cannot use this feature on that undead again. On a failure, it becomes friendly and obeys your commands until you use this feature again. An undead with Intelligence 8 or higher has advantage on the save; if an undead with Intelligence 12 or higher fails, it can repeat the saving throw at the end of every hour until it succeeds and breaks free.
The gold and time you must spend to copy a transmutation spell into your spellbook are halved.

You can temporarily alter one nonmagical object made entirely of wood, stone (not gemstone), iron, copper, or silver into another of those materials. For each 10 minutes you spend performing the procedure, you can transform up to 1 cubic foot of material. After 1 hour, or until you lose your concentration (as if you were concentrating on a spell), the material reverts to its original substance.

After 8 hours, create a stone and choose one benefit for its bearer: darkvision out to 60 feet; speed increased by 10 feet while unencumbered; proficiency in Constitution saving throws; or resistance to acid, cold, fire, lightning, or thunder damage (choose the damage type when selecting this benefit). Each time you cast a transmutation spell of 1st level or higher while the stone is on your person, you can change its benefit. Creating a new stone makes the previous one cease functioning.

Add polymorph to your spellbook if it is not already there. You can cast polymorph once without expending a spell slot; when you cast it this way, you can target only yourself and transform into a beast with challenge rating 1 or lower. After using this feature, you cannot use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

As an action, consume the magic stored in your Transmuter's Stone and choose one effect; the stone is destroyed and cannot be remade until you finish a long rest. Major Transformation changes one nonmagical object no larger than a 5-foot cube into another nonmagical object of similar size and mass and equal or lesser value after 10 minutes of handling. Panacea removes all curses, diseases, and poisons from a creature you touch with the stone and restores all its hit points. Restore Life casts raise dead on a creature you touch without a spell slot or needing the spell in your spellbook. Restore Youth reduces a willing creature's apparent age by 3d10 years (minimum 13) without extending its lifespan.

You always have the Oath of Devotion spells prepared at the relevant paladin levels: 3rd protection from evil and good, sanctuary; 5th lesser restoration, zone of truth; 9th beacon of hope, dispel magic; 13th freedom of movement, guardian of faith; 17th commune, flame strike. They do not count against your prepared paladin spells. If an oath spell does not normally appear on the paladin spell list, it is a paladin spell for you.

As an action, use your Channel Divinity to imbue one weapon you are holding with positive energy for 1 minute. Add your Charisma modifier (minimum +1) to attack rolls with it. It emits bright light in a 20-foot radius and dim light for another 20 feet, and becomes magical if it was not already. You can end the effect on your turn as part of another action; it also ends if you stop holding or carrying the weapon or fall unconscious.

As an action, use your Channel Divinity to present your holy symbol and speak a prayer censuring fiends and undead. Each fiend or undead within 30 feet that can see or hear you must make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, it is turned for 1 minute or until it takes damage. A turned creature must spend its turns trying to move as far away from you as possible and cannot willingly move to a space within 30 feet of you. It also cannot take reactions; for its action, it can use only Dash or try to escape an effect that prevents it from moving. If there is nowhere to move, it can use Dodge.
You and friendly creatures within 10 feet of you cannot be charmed while you are conscious. At paladin level 18, the aura's range becomes 30 feet.
You are always under the effects of protection from evil and good.

As an action, emanate an aura of sunlight for 1 minute. Bright light shines from you in a 30-foot radius and dim light for another 30 feet. An enemy that starts its turn in the bright light takes 10 radiant damage. For the duration, you have advantage on saving throws against spells cast by fiends or undead. Once used, recharge after a long rest.

Always have the oath spells prepared: 3rd ensnaring strike, speak with animals; 5th moonbeam, misty step; 9th plant growth, protection from energy; 13th ice storm, stoneskin; 17th commune with nature, tree stride. If an oath spell does not normally appear on the paladin spell list, it is a paladin spell for you. These spells do not count against the number of paladin spells you can prepare.

name.es: Canalizar Divinidad: Ira de la Naturaleza

features.description: As an action, use Channel Divinity to cause spectral vines to reach for one creature you can see within 10 feet. The creature must succeed on a Strength or Dexterity saving throw (its choice) or be restrained. While restrained by the vines, it repeats the saving throw at the end of each of its turns. On a success, it frees itself and the vines vanish.

name.es: Canalizar Divinidad: Ahuyentar a los Infieles

features.description: As an action, use your Channel Divinity to present your holy symbol and speak a prayer. Each fey or fiend within 30 feet of you that can hear you must make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, it is turned for 1 minute or until it takes damage. A turned creature must spend its turns trying to move as far away from you as possible and cannot willingly move to a space within 30 feet of you; it also cannot take reactions, and can use only the Dash action or try to escape an effect preventing movement. If there is nowhere to move, it can use the Dodge action. If the creature's true form is concealed by an illusion, shapeshifting, or another effect, that form is revealed while it is turned.
Starting at paladin level 7, you and friendly creatures within 10 feet of you have resistance to damage from spells. At paladin level 18, the aura's range increases to 30 feet.

When you are reduced to 0 hit points and are not killed outright, you can drop to 1 hit point instead. Once you use this benefit, you cannot use it again until you finish a long rest. You also suffer none of the drawbacks of old age and cannot be aged magically.

As an action, transform for 1 minute. At the start of each of your turns, regain 10 hit points; paladin spells with a casting time of 1 action can be cast as a bonus action; and enemy creatures within 10 feet have disadvantage on saving throws against your paladin spells and Channel Divinity options. Once used, recharge after a long rest.

Always have the oath spells prepared: 3rd bane, hunter's mark; 5th hold person, misty step; 9th haste, protection from energy; 13th banishment, dimension door; 17th hold monster, scrying. If an oath spell does not normally appear on the paladin spell list, it is a paladin spell for you. These spells do not count against the number of paladin spells you can prepare.

As an action, present your holy symbol and use Channel Divinity to choose one creature you can see within 60 feet. It must make a Wisdom saving throw unless it is immune to being frightened. Fiends and undead have disadvantage on this save. On a failed save, the creature is frightened for 1 minute or until it takes any damage; while frightened, its speed is 0 and it cannot benefit from any bonus to its speed. On a successful save, its speed is halved for 1 minute or until it takes any damage.

As a bonus action, use your Channel Divinity to utter a vow of enmity against a creature you can see within 10 feet. For 1 minute, you have advantage on attack rolls against it. The effect ends early if the creature drops to 0 hit points or falls unconscious.
When you hit a creature with an opportunity attack, you can move up to half your speed immediately after the attack as part of the same reaction. This movement doesn't provoke opportunity attacks.
When a creature under your Vow of Enmity makes an attack, you can use your reaction to make a melee weapon attack against that creature if it is within your weapon's reach.

At paladin level 20, as an action, transform for 1 hour. You gain a flying speed of 60 feet and emanate an aura of menace in a 30-foot radius. The first time an enemy creature enters the aura or starts its turn there during a battle, it must make a Wisdom saving throw or become frightened of you for 1 minute or until it takes any damage. Attack rolls against a creature frightened by this aura have advantage. Once used, this feature cannot be used again until you finish a long rest.
Use the bonus action granted by Cunning Action to make a Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) check, use thieves' tools to disarm a trap or open a lock, or take the Use an Object action.
Climbing no longer costs you extra movement, and when you make a running jump, increase the distance by a number of feet equal to your Dexterity modifier.
You have advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks if you move no more than half your speed on the same turn.
You ignore all class, race, and level requirements on the use of magic items.

You can take two turns during the first round of any combat. You take your first turn at your normal initiative and your second at your initiative minus 10. You cannot use this feature when surprised.
At 1st level, your hit point maximum increases by 1 and increases by 1 again whenever you gain a sorcerer level. While not wearing armor, your AC equals 13 + your Dexterity modifier.

At 1st level, choose one type of dragon as your ancestor; its associated damage type is used by later features: black—acid, blue—lightning, brass—fire, bronze—lightning, copper—acid, gold—fire, green—poison, red—fire, silver—cold, or white—cold. You can speak, read, and write Draconic. When making a Charisma check while interacting with dragons, double your proficiency bonus if it applies to the check.

When you cast a spell that deals damage of the type associated with your draconic ancestry, add your Charisma modifier to one damage roll of that spell. As part of casting such a spell, you can also spend 1 sorcery point to gain resistance to that damage type for 1 hour.

As a bonus action, sprout dragon wings from your back, gaining a flying speed equal to your current speed. You cannot manifest the wings while wearing armor unless the armor is made to accommodate them; they last until you dismiss them as a bonus action.

As an action, spend 5 sorcery points to exude an aura of awe or fear (your choice) to a distance of 60 feet. For 1 minute or until you lose concentration (as if concentrating on a spell), each hostile creature that starts its turn in the aura must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or be charmed (awe) or frightened (fear) until the aura ends. A creature that succeeds on this saving throw is immune to your aura for 24 hours.

At 3rd level, learn three maneuvers of your choice and gain four superiority dice, which are d8s. Spend a die to use a maneuver; only one maneuver can be used per attack. The save DC for a maneuver is 8 + proficiency bonus + your choice of Strength or Dexterity modifier. Regain all spent dice after a short or long rest. Learn two additional maneuvers at fighter levels 7, 10, and 15; you may replace one known maneuver whenever you learn new ones. Gain a fifth die at level 7 and a sixth at level 15; dice become d10s at level 10 and d12s at level 18.
Gain proficiency with one type of artisan's tools of your choice.

When you take the Attack action on your turn, you can forgo one attack and use a bonus action to direct a companion to strike. Choose a friendly creature that can see or hear you and expend one superiority die. The chosen creature can immediately use its reaction to make one weapon attack, adding the superiority die to the attack's damage roll if it hits.

When you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can expend one superiority die to attempt to disarm it. Add the die to the attack's damage roll; the target must make a Strength saving throw. On a failure, it drops one item of your choice that it is holding, and the item lands at its feet.

When you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can expend one superiority die to distract it. Add the die to the attack's damage roll. The next attack roll against the target made by an attacker other than you has advantage if made before the start of your next turn.
When you move, you can expend one superiority die, roll it, and add the result to your AC until you stop moving.

As a bonus action on your turn, you can expend one superiority die to feint, choosing one creature within 5 feet of you as the target. You have advantage on your next attack roll against that creature this turn. If that attack hits, add the superiority die to its damage roll.

When you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can expend one superiority die to attempt to goad it into attacking you. Add the die to the attack's damage roll; the target must make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failure, it has disadvantage on attack rolls against targets other than you until the end of your next turn.
When you make a melee weapon attack on your turn, you can expend one superiority die to increase your reach for that attack by 5 feet. If the attack hits, add the superiority die to its damage roll.

When you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can expend one superiority die to maneuver one of your comrades into a more advantageous position. Add the die to the attack's damage roll and choose a friendly creature that can see or hear you. That creature can use its reaction to move up to half its speed without provoking opportunity attacks from the target of your attack.

When you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can expend one superiority die to attempt to frighten the target. Add the die to the attack's damage roll; the target must make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failure, it is frightened of you until the end of your next turn.
When another creature damages you with a melee attack, you can use your reaction and expend one superiority die to reduce the damage by the number rolled on the die + your Dexterity modifier.

When you make a weapon attack roll against a creature, you can expend one superiority die and add it to the roll. You can use this maneuver before or after making the attack roll, but before any effects of the attack are applied.

When you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can expend one superiority die to attempt to drive it back. Add the die to the attack's damage roll. If the target is Large or smaller, it must make a Strength saving throw; on a failure, you push it up to 15 feet away from you.

On your turn, you can use a bonus action and expend one superiority die to bolster a companion's resolve. Choose a friendly creature that can see or hear you. It gains temporary hit points equal to the superiority die roll + your Charisma modifier.

When a creature misses you with a melee attack, you can use your reaction and expend one superiority die to make a melee weapon attack against it. If you hit, add the superiority die to the attack's damage roll.

When you hit a creature with a melee weapon attack, you can expend one superiority die to damage another creature with the same attack. Choose a different creature within 5 feet of the original target and within your reach. If the original attack roll would hit the second creature, it takes damage equal to the superiority die roll, of the same type dealt by the original attack.

When you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can expend one superiority die to attempt to knock it down. Add the die to the attack's damage roll. If the target is Large or smaller, it must make a Strength saving throw; on a failure, it is knocked prone.

If you spend at least 1 minute observing or interacting with a creature outside combat, you can learn whether it is your equal, superior, or inferior in two characteristics of your choice from this list: Strength score, Dexterity score, Constitution score, Armor Class, current hit points, total class levels (if any), or fighter class levels (if any).
At fighter level 10, your superiority dice become d10s. At fighter level 18, they become d12s.
When you roll initiative and have no superiority dice remaining, regain one superiority die.

At 3rd level, you bond with a beast no larger than Medium and with challenge rating 1/4 or lower; the feature imposes no general restriction on a flying or swimming speed. Add your proficiency bonus to the beast's AC, attack rolls, damage rolls, and to saving throws and skills in which it is proficient. Its hit point maximum is its normal maximum or four times your ranger level, whichever is higher; it can spend Hit Dice during a short rest as normal. The beast acts on your initiative, but takes no action unless you command it to. You can verbally direct its movement without an action; using your action, you can command it to take the Attack, Dash, Disengage, or Help action. Once you have Extra Attack, when you command it to take the Attack action, you can make one weapon attack yourself. While traveling through your favored terrain with only the beast, you can move stealthily at a normal pace. If you are incapacitated or absent, the beast acts on its own, focusing on protecting you and itself; it can use its reaction without a command. If it dies, you can spend 8 hours magically bonding with another beast that is not hostile to you, either the same type as before or a different type.

Beginning at ranger level 7, on a turn when your companion does not attack, you can use a bonus action to command it to Dash, Disengage, or Help. Its attacks count as magical for overcoming resistance and immunity to nonmagical attacks and damage.
At ranger level 11, when you command your companion to take the Attack action, it can make two attacks or use its Multiattack action if it has one.
At ranger level 15, when you cast a spell that targets only yourself, you can also affect your companion with it if the beast is within 30 feet of you.

Immediately after you cast a sorcerer spell of 1st level or higher, the DM can have you roll a d20. On a roll of 1, roll on the Wild Magic Surge table to create a magical effect. If the result is a spell, it is too wild to be affected by your Metamagic; if it normally requires concentration, it does not require concentration in this case and lasts for its full duration. The DM decides whether to call for this d20 roll; a surge is not automatic after every qualifying spell.

Once per long rest, you can gain advantage on one attack roll, ability check, or saving throw. Any time before you regain the use of this feature, the DM can have you roll on the Wild Magic Surge table immediately after you cast a sorcerer spell of 1st level or higher; when the DM does so, you regain the use of Tides of Chaos.

When another creature you can see makes an attack roll, ability check, or saving throw, you can use your reaction and spend 2 sorcery points to roll 1d4 and apply the number as a bonus or penalty to the creature's roll. You can do so after the creature rolls but before the effects of the roll occur.
When rolling on the Wild Magic Surge table, roll twice and choose either result.
Once per turn, when you roll damage for a spell and any damage die shows its maximum value, choose one of those dice, roll it again, and add the new result to the damage.

When you enter a rage, you can choose to enter a frenzy. If you do, for the duration of that rage you can make one melee weapon attack as a bonus action on each of your turns after the turn when you entered the frenzy. When the rage ends, you suffer one level of exhaustion (2014 rules).
While raging, you cannot be charmed or frightened. If either condition is already affecting you when you enter your rage, its effect is suspended for the rage.

As an action, choose one creature you can see within 30 feet. If it can see or hear you, it must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw (DC 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Charisma modifier) or be frightened of you until the end of your next turn. On subsequent turns, you can use your action to extend the effect on that frightened creature until the end of your next turn. The effect ends if the creature ends its turn out of your line of sight or more than 60 feet away from you. If the creature succeeds on its saving throw, you cannot use this feature on it again for 24 hours.
When you take damage from a creature within 5 feet of you, you can use your reaction to make a melee weapon attack against it.
At 3rd level, you can cast beast sense and speak with animals, but only as rituals.

At 3rd level, choose a totem animal; its benefit applies while you rage. Bear: while raging, you have resistance to all damage except psychic. Eagle: while raging and not wearing heavy armor, other creatures have disadvantage on opportunity attacks against you, and you can use Dash as a bonus action on your turn. Elk: while raging and not wearing heavy armor, your walking speed increases by 15 feet. Tiger: while raging, your long-jump distance increases by 10 feet and your high-jump distance by 3 feet. Wolf: while raging, your allies have advantage on melee attack rolls against creatures within 5 feet of you that are hostile to you. The feature calls for a physical totem object; its form and associated animal can be chosen to fit your homeland, and some barbarians develop minor physical traits reminiscent of their totem.

At 6th level, choose a totem animal, which may differ from your 3rd-level choice. Bear: your carrying capacity (including maximum load and maximum lift) doubles, and you have advantage on Strength checks made to push, pull, lift, or break objects. Eagle: you can see up to 1 mile away without difficulty, discern fine details as if looking no more than 100 feet away, and suffer no disadvantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks in dim light. Elk: whether mounted or on foot, your travel pace is doubled, as is the travel pace of up to ten companions while they are within 60 feet of you and you are not incapacitated. Tiger: gain proficiency in two of Athletics, Acrobatics, Stealth, or Survival. Wolf: you can track other creatures while traveling at a fast pace, and you can move stealthily while tracking at a normal pace.
Cast commune with nature as a ritual; a spiritual version of one of your chosen totem animals appears to convey the information.

At 14th level, choose a totem animal, which may differ from earlier choices; its benefit applies while raging. Bear: while raging, creatures within 5 feet of you that are hostile to you have disadvantage on attack rolls against targets other than you or another barbarian with this feature. An enemy is immune to this effect if it cannot see or hear you, or if it cannot be frightened. Eagle: while raging, gain a flying speed equal to your current walking speed; if you end your turn in the air and nothing else is holding you aloft, you fall. Elk: as a bonus action during your move while raging, move through the space of a Large or smaller creature; it must make a Strength saving throw (DC 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Strength modifier) or be knocked prone and take 1d12 + your Strength modifier bludgeoning damage. Tiger: while raging, if you move at least 20 feet in a straight line toward a Large or smaller target immediately before making a melee weapon attack against it, you can use a bonus action to make another melee weapon attack against it. Wolf: while raging, you can use a bonus action on your turn to knock a Large or smaller creature prone when you hit it with a melee weapon attack.
